note: The How to play card (docs/ui/hud-spec.md section 17): every word it shows, as data, so a tone change or a translation is a data swap. Pages hold items; an item is an icon (drawn by UiHowto) and a line. The controls page draws each row's key or button from the player's own layout (data/input/layouts.json, through UiGlyphs), and skips a row the layout does not bind. Orb's direction for the copy: the player IS the fighter. Say bluntly what they control (fly, dodge, guard, light or heavy, power, signature, specials, transform) and what is automatic (no combo inputs: the blows and combos play out on their own). Never frame the player as directing someone else; 'director' and 'strategist' are internal words.
title: HOW TO PLAY
reopen: Open this again from the pause menu or F1.

items.text: You are the fighter. Fly, dodge, guard, hit light or heavy, hold power, call your signature, transform. Transform when the prompt shows: you hit harder for the rest of the match.
No combo inputs to learn. Blows and combos play out on their own.
No health bars. Damage shows on the bodies.
A finishing move ends the fight, not a clock.
Nothing held: you fight with martial arts. Hold a shoulder button to change stance.
Each stance changes what your four buttons do: see Stances.
Fly
Light
Heavy
Signature (45 Charge)
Action (grab, throw: it depends on your stance)
Energy (hold; Settings can make it a toggle)
items.text_toggle: Energy (toggle; Settings can make it hold)

items.text: Guard (hold)
Dodge (tap), sprint (hold)
Power (hold to charge)
Specials
Transform (when the prompt shows)
Escape (get out of a fight)
Pause
Two on one keyboard: P1 has the left keys, P2 the right (I J K L to fly). This page shows yours.

touch_items.text: Left thumb: the stick. Flick to dodge, push out to sprint.
Attack: tap light, hold heavy, swipe up for your signature.
Transform: the button pulses when a form is ready.

items.text: Hold {defensive} (defensive), {energy} (energy), {charging} (charging) or {manoeuvre} (manoeuvre) to change stance. Let go and you are back in martial arts.
Use the stance buttons to change stance. Let go and you are back in martial arts.
Tap a stance button to use it for your next blow, or hold it to stay in the stance.
The game picks your stance for you.
A ring flashes when part of a body is hurt more, and a card says which.
A faint ring: he is nearly beaten. A finishing move can end it.
Watch your rival: his stance and his finishing move.
Get an opening, then press launch. It recharges; until then it only hits hard.
Finishing-move rings: hold or slip. Guard a launch, dodge a close-up attack, press to answer a beam.
The box at the top counts the damage to the world.
The strip is the whole planet. It wraps.
About this game and its licenses: Pause, then About.

How this game was made. Orb Combat EX is a one-person project: Orb directs it and builds it with AI tools. AI tools wrote the game's code and drafted its art, animation data, dialogue, UI text and design documents.
The music was generated with Suno.
There is no voice acting. Character vocal sounds are synthesised by code.

Nothing in the game is generated by AI while you play: its procedural systems (planets, fight choreography, the computer-controlled opponent) are ordinary code, not AI models. Orb directs the project, makes the creative decisions, and tests and plays the game. No part of this game is described as human-made unless this page says so.
